frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes a single positive evaluative quality: the state of being — or the act of rendering — GOOD / FINE / FAIR / COMELY / EXCELLENT. It marks the "good/fine" pole of an evaluative axis whose opposite pole the Quran names with سوء / سيّئة (and, aesthetically, قبح). This one quality surfaces both aesthetically (beauty, comeliness, fairness) and morally/qualitatively (goodness, excellence, best-ness); the two are not separate meanings but the same evaluative fineness applied to appearance versus conduct/outcome.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes a single positive evaluative quality: the state of being — or the act of rendering — GOOD / FINE / FAIR / COMELY / EXCELLENT. It marks the "good/fine" pole of an evaluative axis whose opposite pole the Quran names with سوء / سيّئة (and, aesthetically, قبح). This one quality surfaces both aesthetically (beauty, comeliness, fairness) and morally/qualitatively (goodness, excellence, best-ness); the two are not separate meanings but the same evaluative fineness applied to appearance versus conduct/outcome.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every ح-س-ن word in the packet says that something is good/fine, is made good/fine, or is the best/finest. The forms distribute the same core quality across grammatical slots. ADJ حَسَن/حِسَان predicates the quality of a noun: رزقًا حسنًا "goodly provision" (11:88, 16:67, 22:58), خيراتٌ حِسانٌ "fair maidens" (55:70), عبقريٍّ حِسانٍ "fine carpets" (55:76), الأسماء الحُسنى "the finest names" (7:180, 17:110, 20:8, 59:24), أسوةٌ حسنةٌ "a good example" (33:21, 60:4, 60:6), قرضًا حسنًا "a goodly loan" (2:245, 57:11, 64:17, 73:20). N حَسَنة nominalizes it as "a good thing/deed," repeatedly and explicitly opposed to سيّئة (13:22, 41:34, 4:78-79, 27:46, 28:54, 7:168 بالحسنات والسيّئات). The elative أَحْسَن = "better/finest/best" (أحسن القصص 12:3, أحسن الحديث 39:23, أحسن تقويم 95:4, بالتي هي أحسن 6:152/17:34/29:46). The superlative feminine الحُسْنَى = "the best (reward/outcome)" (10:26, 53:31, 92:6/92:9, 4:95, 57:10). حُسْن = "goodness/fineness" (حسنُ مآب 13:29, حُسنُهنّ "their beauty" 33:52). The Form-IV verb أَحْسَن and its verbal noun إِحْسَان = "to make good / to do good / excellence" (أحسن كل شيء خلقه 32:7, فأحسن صوركم 40:64/64:3, أحسن مثواي 12:23, بالوالدين إحسانًا, هل جزاء الإحسان إلا الإحسان 55:60), and the participle مُحْسِن/المُحْسِنِين = "doer(s) of good." The stative Form-I حَسُنَ = "is/became good/excellent" (حَسُنَت مرتفقًا 18:31, حَسُنَت مستقرًّا 25:76, حَسُنَ أولئك رفيقًا 4:69). Subtract the form and the constant is always the good/fine/excellent quality.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: ROOT residue = the good/fine/excellent quality itself. FORM supplies the rest: Form I حَسُنَ = stative "be good"; the elative pattern أَفْعَل/فُعْلَى (أحسن / الحُسنى) supplies "-er/-est" (comparison/superlative) on top of the quality, not the quality; Form IV أَحْسَنَ/إحسان supplies the causative-agentive "make/do" wrapper (render good, act well); the participle مُحْسِن supplies agency (one who does good); the ة-nominal حَسَنة/حُسْن supplies thing/abstraction ("a good deed", "goodness"). CONSTRUCTION supplies orientation: بالوالدين إحسانًا, أحسنَ بي, أحسنَ إليك = goodness directed toward a beneficiary; بالتي هي أحسن = instrumental "in the finest manner"; أحسنَ صورَكم/كلَّ شيء = goodness imparted to a made object. CONTEXT supplies the aesthetic-vs-moral coloring (a face's beauty in 33:52, comely maidens in 55:70, versus moral good deeds vs سيّئة). None of these is the residue; strip them and "good/fine/excellent" always remains.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 18:104 (وهم يحسبون أنهم يُحسنون صُنعًا, "they reckon they are doing good in work") and 35:8 (فرآه حسنًا, an evil deed that its doer "sees as good/fine"). Here the good-quality is FALSELY attributed to something actually bad. This does not break presence: the root still denotes exactly the "good/fine" quality — it is merely predicated wrongly (subjectively claimed/perceived). The word means "good"; the falsehood lies in the predication, not in a shift of the root's contribution. A second, distinctness-testing case is the recurring pairing خيرٌ وأحسن (17:35, 4:59) and أحسن مقيلًا / خير مستقرًّا (25:24), where أحسن can look synonymous with خير — but the very co-occurrence shows the Quran treats them as distinct facets (benefit/welfare = خير, fineness/excellence = أحسن), which supports rather than dissolves the residue.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: That ح-س-ن is not one contribution but two: (a) an aesthetic root "beauty/fairness/comeliness" (the face حُسنهنّ 33:52, fair maidens حِسان 55:70, fine carpets 55:76, the beautiful names الحُسنى) and (b) a moral root "good deed / doing good" (حَسَنة opposed to سيّئة, إحسان, المحسنين). Rebuttal: the same elative and Form-IV apparatus operates identically across both fields — أحسن names the best narrative (12:3), the best forms/shapes صوركم (40:64), AND the best deed (46:16); حَسُنَ predicates a resting-place (18:31) exactly as حَسَن predicates conduct; and both fields take the identical antonym structure (حسنة/حُسن ⇄ سيّئة/سوء). One evaluative "fine/good" quality, freely applied to appearance or to conduct/outcome, generates all cases; positing two roots is unmotivated because nothing in the morphology or the opposition structure separates them.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Residue is distinct from nearest evaluative roots, and the Quran itself draws the lines. خير (benefit/welfare/"better-in-good") co-occurs with أحسن precisely because they differ — خيرٌ وأحسن تأويلًا (17:35), خيرٌ مستقرًّا وأحسنُ مقيلًا (25:24): خير = the beneficial, أحسن = the finer/more excellent in quality or form. صلح (soundness/rightness/fittingness) opposes فساد, whereas حسنة opposes سيّئة — حسن is fineness/goodness, not fitness. طيّب (wholesome/pleasant/agreeable) is an intrinsic pleasantness, distinct from the evaluative excellence of حسن (note 46:16 / 40:64 where طيّبات and حسن co-occur without merging). The falsifiable core: any occurrence where ح-س-ن denoted something neutral or bad without a perception/claim frame would sink universal presence; none exists in the 194.
internal_discovery.rationale: All 194 confirmed occurrences were assessed and every one carries the "good/fine/fair/excellent" quality after subtracting form and construction. The set is internally coherent and self-validating: the systematic حسنة⇄سيّئة (good⇄evil) opposition (13:22, 41:34, 4:78-79, 27:46, 28:54, 7:168) fixes حسن as the positive evaluative pole; the elative/superlative forms (أحسن, الحُسنى) transparently stack "-er/-est" onto that same quality; the Form-IV verb and إحسان add a "make/do good" wrapper without altering the residue; the three stative Form-I tokens (18:31, 25:76, 4:69) show the bare "is good/excellent." The aesthetic tokens (beauty of a face 33:52, fair maidens 55:70, fine carpets 55:76, the finest names) and the moral tokens unify under one evaluative fineness, evidenced by the shared elative/Form-IV apparatus and shared antonym. Distinctiveness against خير, صلح, and طيّب holds and is corroborated by the Quran's own contrastive co-occurrences. The only apparent resisters (18:104, 35:8) are false-predication cases in which the root still means "good," so presence is not forced. Strength is STRONG for universal presence; the single caveat lowering it from unqualified is the breadth of the residue (aesthetic + moral), which is the root's genuine lexical content rather than analytic vagueness.

adversarial_verification.notes: Full coverage: all 194 occurrences accounted for across 5 form classes (ADJ 32, N 87, N(IV) 51, V 3, V(IV) 21). Adversarial refutation attempted on every occurrence; none resists. After subtracting form (elative aHsan = best/finer; Form IV verb/participle muHsin/iHsAn = do-good/render-good/kindness), construction (aHsana X = do X well; al-Husnaa substantivized = the best outcome/reward), and context, every occurrence contributes the single positive evaluative 'good/fine/fair/comely/excellent/best' pole. Probed hard cases and all reconcile at root level: 18:104 yuHsinuuna Suncan (self-deceived 'doing good') and 35:8 fara'Ahu Hasanan (evil made to seem good) — the misperception is context, the word still contributes 'good'; 19:74 aHsanu aTAthan (wicked yet 'finer in goods') — aesthetic/material fineness pole present; al-Husnaa as fixed Paradise-reward (16:62, 9:107, 41:50, 92:6/9) is literally the elative of the pole, 'reward' supplied by construction. Axis anchoring is textual, not lexical: Hasana repeatedly paired against sayyi'a/suu' (11:114, 13:6, 27:46, 28:54, 41:34, 7:95, 3:120, 4:78-79, 27:11). Distinctiveness holds vs khayr (benefit), SAliH (soundness), Tayyib (pure) — decisively, khayr and aHsan co-occur within single verses (17:35, 4:59, 25:24, 16:30), so the text treats them as near but non-identical: Hsn residue = intrinsic evaluative fineness/comeliness (appearance or conduct), non-empty and distinctive. Falsifiable in principle (no neutral, negative, or non-evaluative/homographic sense such as counting appears) yet not falsified. Universal presence holds under non-negotiable root unity.

occurrence_dispositions.note: Disbelievers falsely claim الحُسْنَى (the best reward) is theirs; the falsity lies in the attribution, not the word, which still denotes the best/finest outcome — the good/fine quality is present.
يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا — subjects merely think they do well; the verb's semantic core is precisely 'doing good/well,' which is present regardless of the ironic framing that they are in fact not.
